page.layout: One page of running text. Running head at top, with the page number 71 beside it. Body in one column of paragraphs, with a centred italic rubric. Below that, two parallel columns: left THESIS, right ANTITH, then a centred CONCILIATIO label, then two more parallel columns: left "a Ratione", right "b Ratione". Signature centred at the foot. No marginal notes.

main_text.p: anima, vt in subiecto proprio & immediato: In corde, vt in subiecto mediato, & per aliud: quia anima (quæ viin-[?]telligendi prædita est) est in corde.

head.i: Notent hic studiosi obiter Commonefactionem se-quentem.

main_text.p: Denominatio rei fit aut ab interno: vt forma, vel adiuncto interno: aut ab externo, vt causa efficiente, vel adiuncto externo. Aut ab vtroque.
Forma] Deus dicitur infinitus, ab infinitate.
Adiun. inter] Absolomus dicitur pulcher à pulchritu-dine. Aqua est humida per inhærentiam.
Effic.] Sacræ literæ dicuntur diuinæ, quia à Deo pro-fectæ. Agens denominatur ab actione, quæ ab ipso est.

Adi. Extex.] Homo dicitur vestitus, ocreatus, à veste, o-crea. Hoc poculum (vino repletum) est humidum. Spon-gia est humida. Ecclesia est iusta & in se ipsa & extra ipsa. Iustitia in Ecclesia ipsa & subiectiue est & extra ipsam (in Christo) Caro Christi olim ambulantis in terra, & nunc versantis in coelo, dicitur circumscripta & terminata, tum ratione accidentis interni, nempe triplicis dimensionis; tum ratione accidentis externi, nempe loci physici vel [illegible, ~8 letters].

head.i: An proprium, vni per se oppositum, eidem per accidens attribui possit ?

main_text.p: Dum aliquid vni per se conuenit, oppositum eius neque ex accidenti, neque per se eidem convenire poterit. Piccol. grad. 8. cap. 7. Per se creatura, vt caro assumpta à Filio Dei est minor Deo, est finita & circumscripta & in certo Vbi. Non potest igitur ex accidenti simul esse æqualis Deo, incircumscripta & vbique.

head.i: An Distinctio Accidentis in separabile & inseparabile sit proba?

main_text.p: THESIS. Forma seu pulchritudo est accidens a χωρισμοῦ[?], i.e. separabile à corpore. Logici.
ANTITH. Nullum accidens est à subiecto separabile. b Metaphys.
main_text.head: CONCILIATIO.
main_text.p: a Ratione φύσεως[?], seu Defitio-nis, id est, existentia formæ accidentalis in subiecto potest de-finere; quia forma illa potest perire,
b Ratione ipsius ὑπάρ-ξεως[?] seu existentiæ, id est, Nullum accidens seorsum extra subiectum potest exi-stere.

page.notes: Top right corner shows a number "642" that looks like a later manuscript or library pagination, not the printer's page number, so it is left out. The Greek word after "vel" in the Adi. Extex. gloss is not legible on the scan. The Greek after "a" in THESIS and after "a Ratione" are doubtful and marked [?]. "viin-" at the line end is printed this way and may be a printing error for "intel-"; the word after the hyphen is "telligendi". The heading "An Distinctio ... inseparabile" line break is uncertain, and "inseparabile" is marked [?]. "possit ?" has a space before the question mark as printed. The Greek after "b Ratione ipsius" is doubtful. The signature "Eee 4" is read from a small mark and may be off by a letter. Spelling such as "Absolomus", "Defitio-nis", "Piccol." and "Vbi" is kept as printed.
